Express your answer in terms of $h.$

g(h)=\frac{5}{h}sin⁡(\pi +2h).

feedback.worked_solution:
We have the function $f(x)=5sin⁡(2x).$ Notice that we are given the length $h$ of the interval. So, the average rate of change of $f$ over this interval is given by

$$
\frac{Δf}{Δx}=\frac{f(a+h)-f(a)}{h},
$$

with $a=\frac{\pi }{2}.$ Substituting into the formula and simplifying gives

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{Δf}{Δx} & =\frac{f(a+h)-f(a)}{h} \\  & =\frac{f(\frac{\pi }{2}+h)-f(\frac{\pi }{2})}{h} \\  & =\frac{5sin⁡(2(\frac{\pi }{2}+h))-5sin⁡(2\cdot \frac{\pi }{2})}{h} \\  & =\frac{5sin⁡(\pi +2h)-5sin⁡(\pi )}{h} \\  & =\frac{5sin⁡(\pi +2h)-5(0)}{h} \\  & =\frac{5sin⁡(\pi +2h)}{h} \\  & =\frac{5}{h}sin⁡(\pi +2h).\end{aligned}
$$
